title: Broadcast Industry Initiatives Promise To Speed Adoption of ST 2110
body_html:
What Was Announced

The broadcast industry has seen the introduction of initiatives aimed at accelerating the adoption of SMPTE ST 2110, a set of standards for professional media over managed IP networks. These initiatives are designed to facilitate the transition from traditional SDI-based infrastructures to more flexible and scalable IP-based systems, enabling broadcasters to take advantage of the benefits of IP, including greater flexibility, improved scalability, and reduced costs. The announcement highlights the industry's efforts to promote the adoption of ST 2110, which is expected to have a significant impact on the way broadcasters design and operate their facilities.

The Engineering and Operational Significance

The adoption of ST 2110 has significant technical implications for broadcasters, as it enables the use of IP networks to transport video, audio, and metadata, allowing for greater flexibility and scalability in broadcast operations. By using IP, broadcasters can take advantage of the flexibility and scalability of IP networks, which can be easily expanded or reconfigured as needed, and can also be used to support a wide range of applications, including live production, playout, and distribution. The use of ST 2110 also enables the use of advanced technologies such as software-defined networking (SDN) and network functions virtualization (NFV), which can provide greater control and flexibility in managing broadcast networks. Additionally, the adoption of ST 2110 can also enable the use of cloud-based services and virtualized applications, which can provide greater scalability and flexibility in broadcast operations.

The operational significance of ST 2110 lies in its ability to simplify broadcast workflows and reduce the complexity of broadcast operations. By using IP, broadcasters can eliminate the need for traditional SDI routing and distribution equipment, and can instead use IP switches and routers to manage their networks. This can reduce the complexity and cost of broadcast operations, and can also enable broadcasters to take advantage of the flexibility and scalability of IP networks. Furthermore, the use of ST 2110 can also enable the use of advanced monitoring and analytics tools, which can provide greater visibility and control over broadcast operations.

Industry Context

The adoption of ST 2110 is part of a broader trend in the broadcast industry towards the use of IP-based technologies and cloud-based services. This trend is driven by the need for greater flexibility, scalability, and cost-effectiveness in broadcast operations, as well as the need to support new and emerging applications such as OTT and social media. The use of ST 2110 is also consistent with the industry's shift towards software-defined and virtualized technologies, which can provide greater flexibility and scalability in broadcast operations. Other comparable approaches and competing technologies include the use of AES67 for audio over IP, and the use of ABR (adaptive bitrate) streaming for OTT and online video distribution. Additionally, the adoption of ST 2110 is also influenced by the development of new and emerging standards and technologies, such as 5G and edge computing, which are expected to have a significant impact on the broadcast industry in the coming years.

The broadcast industry's adoption of ST 2110 is also influenced by the need to support new and emerging business models, such as subscription-based and advertising-based services. The use of ST 2110 can enable broadcasters to take advantage of these new business models, by providing greater flexibility and scalability in broadcast operations, and by enabling the use of advanced technologies such as personalized advertising and dynamic content insertion. Furthermore, the adoption of ST 2110 can also enable broadcasters to take advantage of new and emerging opportunities, such as the use of artificial intelligence and machine learning in broadcast operations, and the use of cloud-based services and virtualized applications to support broadcast workflows.

Implications for Broadcast and Media Teams

For broadcast and media teams, the adoption of ST 2110 has significant implications for the design and operation of broadcast facilities. Engineers and operations managers should take note of the need to plan and implement IP-based infrastructures, and to ensure that their facilities are compatible with ST 2110. This will require careful planning and evaluation of existing workflows and systems, as well as the development of new skills and expertise in IP networking and software-defined technologies.
